editorialRead.oneLineSummary: different-ai/openwork leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.

OpenHands/OpenHands — No same-day commit after 40 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Watch where an OpenWork Cloud client refreshes its runtime address
dailyInsight.insight: If you evaluate an OpenWork main-branch Cloud build containing its legacy-proxy refactor, watch one harmless reconnect or expiry path: does a client that needs a stable address resolve a fresh signed preview at connection time, while a Web client receives the current preview only when that is the intended route?
dailyInsight.mechanism: OpenWork's public refactor deletes its standalone den-worker-proxy and moves Cloud runtime resolution into a shared worker-access path. The focused evaluation refreshes an expired signed preview, preserves a stable API route for a legacy client, resolves that route to the current preview before forwarding, and rejects a sandbox-controlled health-check redirect.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: An expiring runtime URL and a stable client endpoint answer different operational needs. Treating their handoff as one visible resolution boundary can make a Cloud connection easier to reason about, but the evidence remains public main-branch source and tests rather than release, default-configuration or deployment proof.

actions.audience: Operator or maintainer evaluating an OpenWork Cloud build that uses signed runtime previews
actions.label: Trace one harmless refresh through the connection boundary
actions.instruction: In a disposable Cloud workspace, observe one normal connection and one harmless reconnect after the preview is renewed. Record whether a stable client route resolves the fresh destination at request time, whether an expiring direct preview is not retained as the durable address, and whether an unexpected redirect or unavailable preview fails safely. Do not use this as a credential, security or release-availability test.
actions.effort: 15–30 minutes in a disposable Cloud workspace

receipts.title: refactor(cloud): remove the legacy worker proxy path
receipts.supports: Shows the public main-branch refactor that deletes the standalone proxy, names fresh signed previews as the common Cloud runtime access seam, and adds the shared access and compatibility-path work.

receipts.title: Cloud runtime signed-preview evaluation
receipts.supports: Shows the tested expired-preview refresh, stable legacy route, request-time forwarding to a fresh preview, and redirect refusal described by the watch call.

confidence.basis: The merged public commit, its shared access implementation and its deterministic runtime evaluation agree on the intended split between a stable client route and an expiring signed preview. The call remains a watch because the evidence does not establish a release, default enablement or behavior in a particular Cloud deployment.

dailyInsight.limitation: The receipts do not establish that a released OpenWork build contains the refactor, that signed previews are enabled in every environment, that the behavior performs consistently under load, or that the focused redirect check covers every authentication and network failure path.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise or withdraw the call if public source or a regression shows a legacy stable route retaining a stale preview host, bypassing access resolution when a preview expires, following a sandbox-controlled redirect, or a released contract that materially changes the client-routing model.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for release documentation that specifies preview expiry, stable-client compatibility and user-visible failure behavior, plus public regression tests for renewed credentials and unavailable previews.
